chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have finished your Tawaf, go to the Maqam Ibrahim (Station of Abraham), may the prayers of Allah be upon him, and pray two rak'ahs, placing it in front of you. Recite in the first of them Surah al-Tawhid ["Qul huwa Allahu ahad"] and in the second say "Ya ayyuha al-kafirun". Then perform the Tashahhud, praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask Him to accept from you. And these two rak'ahs are the obligatory prayer; it is not disliked to pray them at any time you wish, at sunrise and at sunset, and do not delay them for the time it takes to perform Tawaf and finish, but pray them.'.

And it is not permissible for anyone to pray these two rak'ahs except at the Maqam; if he prays them elsewhere, he must repeat the prayer. As for the rak'ahs of the voluntary prayers (Nawafil), let him pray them in any place he chooses of the Mosque.

key_terms.سُورَةَ التَّوْحِيدِ: Surah Al-Tawhid (Surah Al-Ikhlas), recited in the first rak'ah
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْكَافِرُونَ: Surah Al-Kafirun, recited in the second rak'ah
key_terms.طَوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.مَقَامَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Maqam Ibrahim, the Station of Abraham near the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: Where and how should the two rak'ahs of prayer after Tawaf be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the two rak'ahs after Tawaf as a confirmed Sunnah or obligatory act (depending on the school of thought) strictly tied to the physical location of the Maqam Ibrahim, distinguishing them from general voluntary prayers. The specific recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Kafirun highlights the theological emphasis on monotheism and purity of creed immediately following the ritual circumambulation. This ruling underscores the spatial sanctity of the Maqam as an extension of the Kaaba's spiritual axis, requiring re-performance if prayed elsewhere.
